intro.text: The youngest princess of Idris, whose father sends her to marry Hallandren's God King in place of her older sister, Vivenna.
A princess of Idris and the new queen of Hallandren, wed to a silent God King she is forbidden to speak to or even look at.
A princess of Idris and queen of Hallandren, who spends her nights secretly teaching her husband, the tongueless God King Susebron, to read and write.
A princess of Idris and queen of Hallandren, who comes through the attack on the palace with her husband, Susebron, as war with Idris is averted.

items.text: The youngest of King Dedelin's four children, Siri grew up in Bevalis with little expected of her: Vivenna was being raised to wed the God King of Hallandren, Ridger would inherit the throne, and Fafen had joined a monastery. Siri skipped her lessons, let her Royal Locks show every mood and handed bright flowers to the town's children. Sent to the kitchens as punishment, she enjoyed working there beside her friend Mab, the cook.

Bound by an old treaty to send a daughter to the God King, Dedelin chose at the last moment to send seventeen-year-old Siri rather than Vivenna. Torn from her carefree life, she spent the carriage ride to T'Telir venting her confusion and anger at her small escort of guards, wishing her better-prepared sister had gone instead.

Hallandren overwhelmed her: forty thousand Lifeless soldiers stood waiting to greet her, and colour covered every street and building. Treledees, the God King's high priest, told her there would be no wedding ceremony. Siri sent her guards home to Idris and went on into the Court of Gods alone.

In the palace, servants scrubbed, dressed and groomed her while Bluefingers, a Pahn Kahl scribe, explained her duties. As the Vessel she must never speak to the God King, meet his eyes or touch him unbidden; each night she was to undress, kneel by his bed and wait for his sign.

Through her wedding night she knelt naked while the God King only watched her, and in the morning she burned the bedsheets as her role required. Bluefingers told her she had no duties, but she was not to leave the palace.

The nights went on the same way. Trapped and frustrated, Siri finally shouted at the God King to get on with it, then dared to look him in the eye. When nothing happened to her, she resolved to stop living in fear.

Presented to the Court of Gods, she was awed by the young-looking God King, whose presence split light into colours; Bluefingers explained that his power came from the Breath Peacegiver had left behind. She also met the god Lightsong, whose joking left her at a loss.

Bit by bit she bent the rules, sitting up to meet the God King's gaze, keeping her shift on and sleeping on the floor. When Treledees hinted that the palace knew what really went on, and Bluefingers said the priests listened at night, she began faking the sounds of lovemaking before falling asleep in the bed.

Bluefingers warned her that giving the God King a child was the worst thing she could do. That night, after her act, the God King, Susebron, loomed over her bed. Her shriek startled him as much as her, and he held out a book of children's stories. She saw that his tongue had been cut out, leaving him a powerless figurehead, and began teaching him to read.

Barred by the scribes from taking history books out of the library, Siri learned what she could from Susebron himself as they wrote to each other through the nights. His view of the world came from his storybook and his priests' lessons; he did not even know how an heir is made. His innocence and quiet defiance drew her to him, and she began to fear that his priests meant him harm.

Seeking answers, she turned to Lightsong. His high priest, Llarimar, told her the last two God Kings had died soon after fathering a son and suggested a storyteller, so she asked Lightsong to summon one. Llarimar's helpfulness made a welcome change from her own priests.

At night she told Susebron about the mountains of Idris and tried to explain Austre and the idea of other religions. He wished she could go home to see the mountains again, but would not believe that his priests wanted him dead.

The storyteller, Hoid, told her of the Manywar and Peacegiver, and said that Idris's royal line descends from the First Returned. Each God King, he said, lives only until he has an heir. Upset, Siri left before Lightsong could see her cry.

After Blushweaver threatened to destroy her if she corrupted Lightsong, Siri traded what she knew with Bluefingers, who admitted he feared for the God King's life. They struck a deal: if things went badly, he would get her and Susebron out of the palace.

Susebron promised he would not leave her, and asked her to grow her hair long and red. When she said people at home had wanted her to be more like her sister, he told her she held so much colour inside that it spilled out around her. He agreed to flee with her to Idris if she could prove his priests meant to kill him.

Growing bolder at court, Siri kept Treledees waiting and told him she knew about Susebron's tongue. She also had her serving women replaced with Pahn Kahl servants, hoping they would help if she and Susebron had to escape.

Reasoning together that the true heir must be a stillborn infant who Returns, not a child of theirs, Siri and Susebron grew ever closer, until one night they consummated their marriage. They had fallen in love.

Confessing their love, they agreed that Susebron should take charge of his kingdom: Siri would tell Lightsong that the God King could not speak, so the gods would demand to hear from him. On her way to the court, priests with Lifeless barred her path, declared that she was pregnant and shut her away under guard.

Alone in her room, she placed her hopes in Susebron, whom she had taught to read and given the will to defy his priests. Then she woke to shouting, and Treledees came in and had soldiers drag her away.

Hauled through the palace to Susebron, Siri realised it was under attack. Bluefingers arrived to lead them to the docks, but remembering Lightsong's advice about seeming average, she saw that the Pahn Kahl were behind the attack. She confronted Bluefingers, and he ran.

As she, Susebron and the priests tried to fight their way out, Treledees told her a God King could hand on Peacegiver's Breath and survive. Then Lifeless cut him down with the other priests, and the couple were taken by Bluefingers, who meant to drive Idris and Hallandren into war.

Bluefingers brought her to a black stone altar, meaning to make her death look like a Hallandren sacrifice. Siri insisted on dying on her feet. As he raised his knife the room burst into colour, and Susebron, his tongue restored, appeared and saved her.

Afterwards she saw Lightsong's body and learned he had given his life to heal Susebron. Vivenna arrived and the sisters were reunited, and with help from Vasher, whom Vivenna brought to him, Susebron moved to stop the Lifeless marching on Idris, and war was averted.

appearance.text: An attractive young woman with the Royal Locks of Idris's royal family: with effort, she can change her hair's colour and length. She seldom bothers to control it, so it follows her moods and is often the bright blonde of happiness.

personality.text: She has long felt she can't measure up to her 'perfect' older sister, Vivenna. Her childhood defiance came partly from wanting attention, which Austrism frowns on, and partly from knowing she could never match Vivenna. She loves colour and acting on a whim.
Hasty and impulsive, she also has an inner steel and a stubborn streak that carry her through life in the Court of Gods, and she learns to hold her hair steady when she faces down Treledees.

items.text: At first Siri takes Lightsong's playful teasing as an insult, but she soon sees he means no harm and warms to him as he helps her through the politics of the Court. She thinks him an odd man, but a good one.
